title: Truncated simplex coend embeds as the skeleton
statement:
Use simplicial sets of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Let $S:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Sets}$ be any small simplicial set and $k\geq0$. Write $\Delta^a_q=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([q],[a])$. Form the simplicial set
$$R_k(S)=\operatorname{coeq}\left(\coprod_{\alpha:[a]\to[b],\ a,b\leq k}S_b\times\Delta^a\rightrightarrows\coprod_{a\leq k}S_a\times\Delta^a\right),$$
where the arrows are induced by $S(\alpha)$ and postcomposition with $\alpha$ on standard simplices. Thus a degree-$q$ representative is $[x,\beta]$, with $x\in S_a$, $a\leq k$, and $\beta:[q]\to[a]$. The map $j_k:R_k(S)\to S$, $[x,\beta]\mapsto S(\beta)x$, is degreewise injective. Its image consists exactly of those simplices whose unique nondegenerate ancestor has dimension at most $k$; equivalently it is the simplicial subset generated by all simplices of dimension at most $k$. The canonical map from $R_k(S)$ to the unrestricted coend $\int^{[a]}S_a\times\Delta^a\cong S$ is $j_k$. These maps and identifications are natural in $S$ and commute with the truncation maps $R_k(S)\to R_{k+1}(S)$.

source.place: Tag 017R, lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets, supplies unique nondegenerate ancestors. Agent truncated-coend normal-form consequence; the exact coend comparison is not stated verbatim by this tag.

proof.text: Use simplicial sets and colimits as in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] and [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. In degree $q$ take the quotient of $\coprod_{a\leq k}S_a\times\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([q],[a])$ by the equivalence relation generated by $[S(\alpha)u,\gamma]=[u,\alpha\gamma]$, for $\alpha:[a]\to[b]$, $a,b\leq k$, $u\in S_b$, and $\gamma:[q]\to[a]$. For $\theta:[p]\to[q]$, the rule $[x,\beta]\mapsto[x,\beta\theta]$ respects each generating relation; identities and composites act as required. This gives the stated coequalizer of simplicial sets: a map out of this quotient is exactly a family of maps from the summands equalizing the two arrows, degree by degree, and commuting with the operators. All unions and relations are small since $S$ is small and finite ordinals and their order maps form a small category. The formula $[x,\beta]\mapsto S(\beta)x$ respects the relation because $S(\gamma)S(\alpha)u=S(\alpha\gamma)u$. It commutes with $\theta$ because $S(\theta)S(\beta)x=S(\beta\theta)x$, so defines the simplicial map $j_k$.

source.place: Tags 016A (definition-simplicial-object), 0175 (definition-terminology-simplicial-sets); agent quotient construction and universal-property check. Colimit universal property: categories.tex, Tag 002F.

proof.text: Fix a representative $[x,\beta]\in R_k(S)_q$ with $x\in S_a$, $a\leq k$, and $\beta:[q]\to[a]$. List the image of $\beta$ in increasing order. This gives an injection $\delta:[c]\hookrightarrow[a]$ and a surjection $\sigma:[q]\twoheadrightarrow[c]$ with $\beta=\delta\sigma$ and $c\leq a\leq k$. Put $w=S(\delta)x\in S_c$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] to $w$, obtaining $w=S(\tau)y$ with $\tau:[c]\twoheadrightarrow[r]$ and $y\in S_r$ nondegenerate. Surjectivity gives $r\leq c\leq k$. The relations for $\delta$ and $\tau$ give $[x,\beta]=[w,\sigma]=[y,\tau\sigma]$. Thus every class has a representative $[y,\rho]$ with $y$ nondegenerate of dimension at most $k$ and $\rho$ surjective. This argument does not require $q\leq k$: the two relations have bounded indices $c,a$ and $c,r$, while $q$ is only the evaluation degree.

source.place: Tag 017R, lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets, statement and proof; agent reduction using the image factorization of an order map and the explicit coend relations.

proof.text: Suppose $j_k$ takes two classes to the same $z\in S_q$. By step 2 choose representatives $[y,\rho]$ and $[y^{\prime},\rho^{\prime}]$ with nondegenerate simplices and surjective maps. Then $z=S(\rho)y=S(\rho^{\prime})y^{\prime}$. The uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] gives equality of their dimensions, their nondegenerate simplices, and their surjections. The two representatives are therefore the same pair and the two classes coincide. This proves degreewise injectivity of $j_k$.

source.place: Tag 017R, lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets, uniqueness of the nondegenerate simplex, its dimension and its degeneracy surjection.

proof.text: By step 2 every image simplex has a decomposition $S(\rho)y$ with $y$ nondegenerate of dimension $r\leq k$, so [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] identifies $y$ as its unique nondegenerate ancestor. Conversely a simplex with ancestor $y\in S_r$, $r\leq k$, and surjection $\rho:[q]\twoheadrightarrow[r]$ is the image of $[y,\rho]$. This proves the exact ancestor description. By step 1 the degreewise image of $j_k$ is closed under every simplicial operator. It contains every $x\in S_a$, $a\leq k$, using $[x,1_{[a]}]$. Any simplicial subset containing these low-dimensional simplices must contain $S(\beta)x$ for every representative $[x,\beta]$ of $R_k(S)$. Hence the image is precisely the smallest such subset, the simplicial subset generated in dimensions at most $k$.

source.place: Tag 017R, lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets; agent consequence for the image, with the generated-subset assertion proved from operator closure.

proof.text: Let $R_\infty(S)$ denote the same quotient with no bound on $a,b$. The construction of step 1 gives a simplicial map $j_\infty:R_\infty(S)\to S$. In degree $q$ its inverse is $z\mapsto[z,1_{[q]}]$: one composite is the identity, and the unrestricted relation for $\beta:[q]\to[a]$ gives $[x,\beta]=[S(\beta)x,1_{[q]}]$, proving the other composite is the identity. For $\theta:[p]\to[q]$ that same relation gives $[z,\theta]=[S(\theta)z,1_{[p]}]$, so these inverses commute with simplicial operators. The canonical inclusion $R_k(S)\to R_\infty(S)$ preserves representatives. Composing it with this explicit unrestricted-coend isomorphism sends $[x,\beta]$ to $S(\beta)x$ and is therefore exactly $j_k$.

source.place: Tag 016A, definition-simplicial-object; agent explicit unrestricted-coend isomorphism and bounded-to-unbounded comparison.

proof.text: For a map of simplicial sets $f:S\to T$, put $R_k(f)[x,\beta]=[f_a(x),\beta]$. Naturality of $f$ gives $f_a(S(\alpha)u)=T(\alpha)f_b(u)$, so this preserves all generating relations. It commutes with simplicial operators, identities and composites directly from its formula. On representatives, $j_{k,T}R_k(f)[x,\beta]=T(\beta)f_a(x)=f_q(S(\beta)x)=f_qj_{k,S}[x,\beta]$. Thus the image identifications are natural, even if $f$ sends nondegenerate simplices to degenerate ones. The truncation map $R_k(S)\to R_{k+1}(S)$ is $[x,\beta]\mapsto[x,\beta]$ with the same formula in the larger quotient. Consequently it commutes with $R_k(f)$ and with the maps to $S$ and to $R_\infty(S)$. The unrestricted isomorphism and its inverse from step 5 commute with $f$ by their formulas as well. These are all the asserted naturality and truncation compatibilities.

source.place: Tag 016A, definition-simplicial-object, and the observation after Tag 017R that nondegenerate splittings need not be functorial; agent representative formulas prove the asserted naturality without assuming a functorial splitting.
